# Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { postmark } from "@/lib/postmark"; await postmark.sendEmail({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", Subject: "Welcome!", HtmlBody: "

Thanks for signing up.

", TextBody: "Thanks for signing up.", MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `outbound` is the default transactional message stream. Keep transactional and broadcast email in separate streams. ## 4. Send with a template Create the template once in the Postmark dashboard, then send it by alias: ```ts await postmark.sendEmailWithTemplate({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", TemplateAlias: "password-reset", TemplateModel: { name: "Ada", action_url: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }, MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `TemplateId` (a number) works in place of `TemplateAlias`. ## 5. Handle errors `sendEmail` returns a promise that rejects with a typed error from `postmark`'s `Errors` export when Postmark refuses the message (inactive recipient, unconfirmed sender, invalid token). Catch it where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Postmark - Built for transactional email: high delivery rates, with bounce and spam handling included. - Templates live in the dashboard, so copy changes do not need a deploy. - Detailed delivery statistics and inbound email parsing come with the same account. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts import { getCurrentUser, listUsers } from "@/lib/users"; export default async function DashboardPage() { const me = await getCurrentUser(); const all = await listUsers(); return (

Dashboard

Signed in as {me?.name ?? "nobody"} ({me?.email ?? "—"})

Team

    {all.map((u) => (
  • {u.name} — {u.email} — joined {u.createdAt}
    • ))}
); }

content.text:
I added Postmark email to Notely: a welcome email when a user is created and a password reset email, both called from `src/lib/users.ts`. Lint, `next build` and `tsc` all pass. I haven't sent a real email or run the new functions; that needs a real Postmark token and sender.

**Why Postmark:** it's built only for transactional email, delivers reliably, and handles bounces and spam complaints for you. Its official `postmark` package has no runtime dependencies. There was also a Postmark guide in `docs/`, which I followed.

**What changed**
- **`src/lib/postmark.ts`**: the Postmark connection is set up the first time an email is sent, not when the module loads. A missing token then only fails that one send instead of breaking every page that touches users. It's marked server-only so the token can't end up in the browser.
- **`src/lib/email.ts`**: `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`, each with an HTML and a plain-text version. User names are escaped before going into the HTML. Each email is tagged (`welcome` / `password-reset`) for Postmark's stats. Link tracking is off for reset emails so Postmark doesn't rewrite the one-time link.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`**:
  - `createUser({ email, name })` cleans up the email, rejects duplicates, saves the user and sends the welcome email. If the email fails, the error is logged and signup still succeeds.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)` creates a random token that expires in 60 minutes. It stores only a hash of the token, cancels any earlier reset link for that user, and emails a link to `/reset-password?token=…`. It does nothing for unknown emails and behaves the same either way, so it can't be used to find out which addresses have accounts.
  - `consumePasswordResetToken(token)` checks the token, deletes it so it can't be reused, and returns the user, or `undefined` if the token is invalid, used or expired.
  - `getUserByEmail` is new.
- **`.env.example`**: `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN`, `POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL` and `APP_URL`, all placeholders. `.gitignore` was ignoring every `.env*` file, so I added `!.env.example` to let this one be committed.
- **Dependencies**: added `postmark` (5.1.0) and `server-only`.

**Still to do**
- **Postmark account:** put a real server token in `.env.local`. The From address has to be a confirmed sender or on a verified domain, or Postmark will reject the email.
- **Missing pages:** nothing calls these functions yet. There's no signup page, no "forgot password" form and no `/reset-password` page, so the link in the reset email currently goes nowhere.
- **No passwords yet:** users don't have passwords in this codebase. `consumePasswordResetToken` tells you whose password to change, but you need password storage before it can actually change anything.
- **Memory only:** users and reset tokens live in memory, like the existing user list. They're lost on restart and not shared between server instances, so both need a database before production.

Nothing is committed.
